**THE JULY HIKE IS LARGELY PRICED OUT — a major change and a correction to the 17 Jul brief.** CME FedWatch as of 18 Jul: **86.7% probability of a HOLD at the 28-29 July FOMC, i.e. ~13.3% hike odds — down from 46.5% on 13 July.** The 17 Jul brief carried 46.5% as current; it is no longer. Crucially the market has NOT turned dovish: **~73% odds of at least one hike by December remain, and only ~1-in-5 odds that rates are unchanged by year-end.** The hike moved OUT past the July meeting, not away. This REMOVES one of the two near-term binaries the 17 Jul brief flagged for the following ten days. Set against genuinely hawkish Fed communication: Chair Warsh's **first congressional testimony (14 July)** pledged a policy 'regime change' and said the Fed has **'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation'**, adding that 'the latest improvement isn't mission accomplished'; he is also the first Chair to submit NOTHING to the dot plot — a deliberate refusal to telegraph that raises rate volatility by design. Waller: the Fed 'must not repeat the mistakes of 2021-22.' Bank of America moved its base case to a series of 2026 hikes. **Fed blackout began ~18 July — no further commentary before 29 July.** Sourcing note: three incompatible readings circulated 13-18 Jul (46.5% / '73%' / 13.3%); resolved as July-meeting vs by-December questions, with 86.7% hold confirmed by two independent aggregators as the current July print. CONFIRMED.

**July hike odds stabilised at ~15.5% (84.5% HOLD) as of 21 July 03:45 EDT** — ticked marginally up from 13.3% on 18 July but nowhere near the 46.5% of 13 July. **The July hike remains largely priced out even as Brent went to $90 and US retail gasoline crossed $4.00/gallon (AAA, up 86 cents y/y).** That combination is the single most important macro fact of the window: **the oil-to-Fed transmission that defined June and early July has gone quiet.** US 10Y rose to **4.60%**; 2Y 3.70%; S&P -0.19% Monday; VIX **down 4.8% to 17.76**. Fed blackout has been in force since ~18 July, so no official commentary before the **29 July decision** — Chair Warsh's 14 July congressional testimony (pledged policy 'regime change,' 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation,' and the first Chair to submit nothing to the dot plot) remains the operative signal. **The political channel is now live in a way it was not: gasoline at $4.00 is being tied explicitly by Axios to midterm exposure, and House Democrats are citing gas prices in their NDAA revolt.** CONFIRMED (CME FedWatch).
